quests.hint: You say this when you meet someone for the first time each day.
quests.explanation: 'Hello' is the most common greeting in English. Use it when you meet someone or answer the phone.
quests.definition: A greeting used when meeting someone.
quests.example: Hello! My name is Sarah. Nice to meet you.
quests.usageExample: The word "HELLO" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You say this when you leave someone or end a conversation.
quests.explanation: 'Goodbye' is used when leaving or ending a conversation. A shorter form is 'bye'.
quests.definition: A farewell said when leaving someone.
quests.example: Goodbye! I will see you again tomorrow.
quests.usageExample: The word "GOODBYE" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You say this when you ask for something politely.
quests.explanation: 'Please' makes requests polite and friendly. Always use it when asking for something.
quests.definition: A word used to make a request politely.
quests.example: Can I have a glass of water, please?
quests.usageExample: The word "PLEASE" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You say this after someone gives you something or helps you.
quests.explanation: 'Thank you' expresses gratitude. It is one of the most important phrases in English communication.
quests.definition: An expression of gratitude toward someone.
quests.example: Thank you so much for helping me carry the bags.
quests.usageExample: The word "THANK YOU" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You say this when you make a mistake or inconvenience someone.
quests.explanation: 'Sorry' expresses apology or regret. Use it when you make a mistake or want to get someone's attention politely.
quests.definition: An expression of apology or regret.
quests.example: Sorry, I am late. The traffic was very bad today.
quests.usageExample: The word "SORRY" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You say this to agree with something or confirm it is true.
quests.explanation: 'Yes' is used to agree, confirm, or accept something. It is the opposite of 'no'.
quests.definition: A word used to agree or confirm something.
quests.example: Yes, I would love to come to your party on Saturday.
quests.usageExample: The word "YES" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You say this to refuse or disagree with something.
quests.explanation: 'No' is used to refuse, disagree, or deny something. It is the opposite of 'yes'.
quests.definition: A word used to refuse or disagree with something.
quests.example: No, thank you. I do not want any more cake.
quests.usageExample: The word "NO" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You ask for this when you are in danger or need assistance.
quests.explanation: 'Help' means to assist someone. You can also shout it when you are in danger.
quests.definition: To assist someone, or a call for assistance.
quests.example: Can you help me find the train station, please?
quests.usageExample: The word "HELP" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Your body needs this liquid every day to survive - think of drinking.
quests.explanation: 'Water' is a clear liquid essential for life. We drink it, cook with it, and clean with it.
quests.definition: A clear liquid that people drink and use for cooking and cleaning.
quests.example: I drink at least eight glasses of water every day.
quests.usageExample: The word "WATER" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You eat this every day - think of meals like lunch or dinner.
quests.explanation: 'Food' refers to anything we eat to get energy and nutrients. Every meal contains food.
quests.definition: Any substance that people eat for energy and nutrition.
quests.example: The food at that Italian restaurant was absolutely delicious.
quests.usageExample: The word "FOOD" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: This is where you live - your house or apartment.
quests.explanation: 'Home' is the place where you live. It can be a house, apartment, or any place you feel safe and comfortable.
quests.definition: The place where you live and feel comfortable.
quests.example: I usually get home from work at around six o'clock.
quests.usageExample: The word "HOME" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Children go here every day to study and learn from teachers.
quests.explanation: 'School' is an institution where children learn reading, writing, mathematics, and other subjects.
quests.definition: A place where children go to learn and study.
quests.example: My daughter starts her first day of school next Monday.
quests.usageExample: The word "SCHOOL" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Someone you enjoy spending time with and trust.
quests.explanation: 'Friend' is a person you like and enjoy spending time with. Friendship is an important part of life.
quests.definition: A person you like, trust, and enjoy spending time with.
quests.example: My best friend and I have known each other since we were five years old.
quests.usageExample: The word "FRIEND" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Think of describing something you enjoy or that is positive.
quests.explanation: 'Good' describes something positive, pleasant, or satisfactory. It is one of the most common adjectives in English.
quests.definition: Having positive qualities; satisfactory or pleasant.
quests.example: She did a very good job on her English presentation.
quests.usageExample: The word "GOOD" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The opposite of good - something negative or unpleasant.
quests.explanation: 'Bad' describes something negative, unpleasant, or of poor quality. It is the opposite of 'good'.
quests.definition: Having negative qualities; unpleasant or of poor quality.
quests.example: The weather was so bad that we cancelled our picnic.
quests.usageExample: The word "BAD" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Think of a feeling when something nice happens - smiling.
quests.explanation: 'Happy' describes a feeling of joy and contentment. When things go well, people feel happy.
quests.definition: Feeling joy and contentment; pleased.
quests.example: She was very happy when she passed her English exam.
quests.usageExample: The word "HAPPY" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The opposite of happy - you might feel this when something goes wrong.
quests.explanation: 'Sad' describes a feeling of unhappiness or sorrow. It is the opposite of 'happy'.
quests.definition: Feeling unhappy or sorrowful; the opposite of happy.
quests.example: He felt very sad when his favourite team lost the match.
quests.usageExample: The word "SAD" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Think of a large elephant or a tall building - not small.
quests.explanation: 'Big' describes something of large size. It is one of the first adjectives children learn in English.
quests.definition: Of large size or amount.
quests.example: They live in a very big house with a beautiful garden.
quests.usageExample: The word "BIG" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Think of an ant or a mouse - not large.
quests.explanation: 'Small' describes something of little size. It is the opposite of 'big'.
quests.definition: Of little size; not large.
quests.example: Could I have a small coffee, please? I do not want a large one.
quests.usageExample: The word "SMALL" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Think of fire or a hot summer day.
quests.explanation: 'Hot' describes a high temperature. We use it for weather, food, drinks, and objects.
quests.definition: Having a high temperature; the opposite of cold.
quests.example: Be careful — the soup is very hot. Wait a few minutes.
quests.usageExample: The word "HOT" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Think of ice or a winter morning - not warm.
quests.explanation: 'Cold' describes a low temperature. It is the opposite of 'hot'. We also use it for illness.
quests.definition: Having a low temperature; the opposite of hot.
quests.example: It is very cold outside today, so wear a warm coat.
quests.usageExample: The word "COLD" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: This is when the sun is up and people are awake and active.
quests.explanation: 'Day' is the period of time when it is light outside. There are seven days in a week.
quests.definition: The period from sunrise to sunset; a 24-hour period.
quests.example: What day is it today? I think it might be Wednesday.
quests.usageExample: The word "DAY" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: This is when it is dark outside and most people are sleeping.
quests.explanation: 'Night' is the period of darkness when the sun has set. People usually sleep at night.
quests.definition: The period of darkness between sunset and sunrise.
quests.example: We stayed up all night talking and watching films.
quests.usageExample: The word "NIGHT" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You use this to get somewhere - think of a car or a bus.
quests.explanation: 'Go' means to move or travel from one place to another. It is one of the most common verbs in English.
quests.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.
quests.example: I go to the supermarket every Saturday morning.
quests.usageExample: The word "GO" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You do this with food to give your body energy.
quests.explanation: 'Eat' means to put food in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it. We eat to stay alive and healthy.
quests.definition: To put food in your mouth and swallow it.
quests.example: I usually eat breakfast before I leave for work.
quests.usageExample: The word "EAT" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You do this with water, juice, or coffee - through your mouth.
quests.explanation: 'Drink' means to take liquid into your mouth and swallow it. It also refers to a liquid you consume.
quests.definition: To take liquid into the mouth and swallow it.
quests.example: Would you like something to drink? Tea or coffee?
quests.usageExample: The word "DRINK" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You do this in bed at night - your body rests and recovers.
quests.explanation: 'Sleep' means to rest with your eyes closed and your mind inactive. Most people sleep for seven to eight hours each night.
quests.definition: To rest with eyes closed in a state of natural unconsciousness.
quests.example: I need to sleep early tonight because I have an exam tomorrow.
quests.usageExample: The word "SLEEP" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You do this with a pen or pencil on paper.
quests.explanation: 'Write' means to form letters and words on paper or a screen. It is an essential communication skill.
quests.definition: To form letters, words, or sentences on paper or a screen.
quests.example: Please write your name and address at the top of the form.
quests.usageExample: The word "WRITE" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You do this with your eyes when you look at words in a book.
quests.explanation: 'Read' means to look at written words and understand their meaning. Reading is essential for education.
quests.definition: To look at written text and understand its meaning.
quests.example: She loves to read novels before going to bed every night.
quests.usageExample: The word "READ" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You use your mouth to do this - communicating with others in English.
quests.explanation: 'Speak' means to use your voice to say words. You are learning English so you can speak it confidently.
quests.definition: To use your voice to say words; to communicate verbally.
quests.example: She can speak three languages: English, French, and Spanish.
quests.usageExample: The word "SPEAK" can be used in many situations.
